forecasts.reason: Theory: an RL-Math edit works in full on any problem set in its own domain, so the 1.5x top-8 edit should be level with RL's vote of 57 on fresh2026. Set slightly below 57 because on hard328 this edit's vote fell short of RL's (214 vs 221).
Theory: in-domain edits work in full, so the per-sample mean equals RL's single-sample 50.5 of 136. Sample 0 already scored 50, and hard328 showed the same match (200.25 vs 200.0).
Theory: math text drives the top input direction, so on hard328 its effect scales with size. At 1x the top-1 edit scored 181; doubling it pushes toward the top-8 1x level of 192 without reaching it.

Same in-domain drive as t08, but at 3x the single direction's norm is about that of top-8 at 1.5x and concentrated in one direction. The board's dial shows overdrive breaks the model (top-8 at 3x scored 117), so the interval is wide on the low side.

Theory: math text drives Math-RL's input subspaces about equally in every layer band (8.1-11.2x). So each third of the layers should carry roughly a third of the all-layer 1.5x gain: base 164 to 203, with some redundancy.
Theory: input drive is similar across layer bands (8.1-11.2x), so layers 11-21 alone carry about a third of the 1.5x edit's gain over the base (164 to 203).
Theory: input drive is similar across layer bands, so layers 22-31 alone carry about a third of the 1.5x edit's gain over the base (164 to 203).
Theory: the edit works in full on MATH-500, which is in-domain, so new samples should repeat the stored 427 of 500 (plain prompt, 1x top-8). The interval allows sample-to-sample spread.

Theory: the RL change acts in full on in-domain math text, so the transplant's gain carries over to the vote. On fresh2026 the 2x transplant's vote led Think-SFT's by 8 (83 vs 75), and Think-SFT's hard328 vote is 241, giving about 247.
Theory: the edit works in full in-domain, so the transplant holds on MATH-500. The 1x transplant scored 467, Think-SFT singles score 457-462, and at 2x more answers finish.

Theory: full in-domain effect gives the 2x transplant about 234 at seed 3,000,000 at the 16,384 cap. Raising the cap to 32,768 should rescue about a quarter of its roughly 54 cut answers, as it did for Think-SFT (23 of 93 right).
Theory: full in-domain effect on MATH-500 puts the 1.5x cue edit at 456. Going to 2x cost 13 problems on hard328 (190 vs 203), so expect a small drop.
